Psychiatry & medication

Psychiatry & Mental Health Medication

Psychiatry focuses on the evaluation and medical treatment of mental health conditions. A psychiatric prescriber may discuss medication, medical contributors, side effects, and how symptoms change over time.

Last updated September 19, 2026 · Editorial policy

What a psychiatric evaluation may include

A prescriber may ask about symptoms, sleep, medical history, medications, substance use, family history, prior treatment, and safety. Depending on the situation, laboratory testing or coordination with primary care may also be considered.

Medication and therapy can be complementary

Some people use medication without therapy, therapy without medication, or both. The right combination depends on the condition, severity, preferences, medical history, and treatment response.

Questions to ask

  • What are the expected benefits and common side effects?
  • How long might it take to notice changes?
  • What should I do if I miss a dose or want to stop?
  • How will we monitor whether the medication is helping?
